content: Raltegravir is classified as an integrase inhibitor and is used in combination with other HIV medications to manage HIV infection. It works by reducing the amount of HIV in the body, which helps the immune system function more effectively. This, in turn, decreases the risk of developing HIV-related complications, such as opportunistic infections or certain cancers, and improves overall quality of life. However, it is important to note that raltegravir is not a cure for HIV infection. To minimize the risk of transmitting HIV to others, it is essential to take all prescribed HIV medications exactly as directed by your healthcare provider. Additionally, you should use effective barrier methods, such as latex or polyurethane condoms or dental dams, during sexual activity as instructed by your doctor. Avoid sharing personal items that may come into contact with blood or bodily fluids, such as needles, syringes, toothbrushes, or razors. Before starting raltegravir, read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist, and review it each time you receive a refill. The dosage of raltegravir is determined based on your medical condition, response to treatment, and any other medications you may be taking. Swallow the medication whole, as directed by the manufacturer. While some similar drugs (immediate-release tablets) can be split or crushed, this should not be done with raltegravir unless specifically instructed by your doctor or pharmacist. Avoid using antacids containing aluminum or magnesium while taking this medication, as they may interfere with its effectiveness. It is crucial to adhere to your prescribed treatment regimen and not to increase, decrease, or stop the medication without consulting your doctor. For optimal results, take raltegravir at evenly spaced intervals. Missing doses or stopping the medication, even for a short time, can lead to a resurgence of the virus and reduce the effectiveness of your treatment. Common side effects of raltegravir may include headache, nausea, and difficulty sleeping. These effects are generally mild, and your doctor has prescribed this medication because they believe the benefits outweigh the risks. As your immune system strengthens, it may begin to fight off previously undetected infections, potentially causing symptoms of these infections to reappear. In some cases, an overactive immune response may occur, which can happen shortly after starting HIV treatment or even months later. Changes in body fat distribution may occur while taking raltegravir, such as increased fat in the upper back and abdomen or decreased fat in the arms and legs. The cause and long-term effects of these changes are not yet fully understood. Serious allergic reactions to raltegravir are rare but can occur. If you experience symptoms of a severe allergic reaction, such as rash, itching, swelling, severe dizziness, or difficulty breathing, seek immediate medical attention. Before taking raltegravir, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you have any allergies or if you are allergic to this medication. Raltegravir may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed, as it may help reduce the risk of transmitting HIV to your baby. Raltegravir can pass into breast milk, so discuss breastfeeding with your doctor. Drug interactions may alter how raltegravir or other medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal supplements, and share it with your healthcare provider. This document does not include all possible drug interactions, so consult your doctor or pharmacist for more information. In the event of an overdose, if someone has severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222 for assistance. While taking raltegravir, regular laboratory and medical tests, such as viral load and T-cell counts, should be conducted to monitor your progress. Attend all scheduled medical and lab appointments to ensure the effectiveness of your treatment. If you miss a dose of raltegravir, take it as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store raltegravir in its original packaging at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep the desiccant (drying agent) in the bottle and tightly close the bottle when not in use. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about raltegravir. It does not guarantee that the medication is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
